analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + CPI + LVMH + CTS (I) + Orsted (dg) + Zurich (I) 13 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities closed lower in very light Columbus Day trading, the lowest-volume session of the year. SPX -5bps to 7807, NDX -44bps to 27245, DJIA +38bps to 51850. 8 of 11 sectors rose (Energy +143bps, Staples +117bps, Comm Svs +97bps), Info Tech -122bps.
European equities closed higher (SXXP +70bps, SX5E +50bps), led by Utilities (+1.3%), Banks (+1.2%) and Food & Bev (+1%) in a defensive tilt (GSXEDEFS +60bps).
The median S&P stock trades 15% below its 52-week high, the worst reading since the dot-com bubble, with recent months particularly weak.

The S&P implied move through Friday's close was about 1% last week (~96bps as of yesterday morning), one of the lowest 1-week implied moves in about 6 years, despite EPS season starting, CPI on Wednesday and several Fed speakers.

Semiconductors were weak, with memory leading lower on China memory progress, follow-through from Korea (KOSPI -365bps) and a turn in flows (the desk was much better for sale across memory and HDDs into the end of last week).

GS expects September core CPI +0.24% m/m (consensus +0.2%), +2.46% y/y (consensus +2.5%), and headline CPI +0.59% m/m (consensus +0.6%) on higher energy prices. This is consistent with a 0.20% rise in September core PCE.

GS cross-asset allocation moves to overweight equities over 3 months and underweight credit over 3 months, overweight bonds over 12 months and tactically overweight cash. Earnings growth supports equities and the valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into Q3 earnings.

Within equities GS stays overweight the US and Asia and underweight Europe, and favours a barbell of global Technology with selective rate-sensitive, high-dividend, low-volatility and bond-proxy equities that could benefit from eventual rate relief.

LVMH 3Q26 sales grew 1% at constant FX, in line with estimates (+1% GSe/Visible Alpha consensus). Fashion and Leather, the key profit driver, fell -5% cFX versus VA consensus -2% and GSe -2.5%, and versus +1% in 2Q26. This was somewhat worse than expectations, which had already fallen in recent weeks, with the Chinese cluster mostly responsible for the sequential slowdown.

GS initiates CTS Eventim at Neutral with a EUR60.15 PT (15% upside). Valuation is near trough, but a re-rating requires confidence in at least mid-single digit organic growth, a defended competitive position and execution on venue and operational initiatives.

GS downgrades Orsted to Neutral on sovereign rates in Europe and the US up c.50-65 bp since late August (c.100 bp YTD), expected underwhelming Q3 results that could drive negative consensus revisions, and a new DKK155 PT (c.15% upside) now below the sector average.

GS reinstates Zurich at Neutral. It has a targeted >9% EPS CAGR (2025-2027) ex. Beazley and guided pro forma mid-single digit EPS uplift from the Beazley deal. 1-year forward consensus P/E has compressed c.2.0x since April 2025, and GS's 2027e P/E of 12.8x is a 0.5x to 0.7x premium to Allianz and Generali respectively.
The power theme has bottomed and is trending upward as GS expected. Consumer experience stocks have underperformed the SPXXAI by about 16pp.

European and US sovereign rates are up c.50-65 bp since late August, Q3 results are expected to be underwhelming with risk of negative consensus revisions, and the new PT upside of c.15% is below the sector average.
Zurich has a targeted >9% EPS CAGR (2025-2027) ex. Beazley, and valuation has de-rated, with a 2027e P/E of 12.8x at a small premium to Allianz and Generali.
3Q26 sales growth of 1% cFX was in line, but Fashion and Leather fell -5% cFX versus consensus of -2%, with Chinese demand driving the slowdown.

Orsted: GS expects Q3 results to be somewhat underwhelming, which could lead to negative consensus earnings revisions.
Zurich: targeted >9% EPS CAGR (2025-2027) ex. Beazley, with guided pro forma mid-single digit EPS uplift from the Beazley transaction.
Q3 US earnings season is starting this week, and GS says the valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into it.
